lines: Yellowing of the eyes that she first noticed while brushing her teeth two days ago.
The patient with known Gilbert syndrome returns for evaluation of recurrent scleral icterus, having presented in January 2020 with a similar episode.
She reports yellowing of the eyes first noticed while brushing her teeth two days ago.
She recently returned home after completing a week-long religious fast during which she limited herself to only water and small portions of food once daily.
She says she feels tired, but attributes this to resuming classes and preparing for final exams at her university.
She denies abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, dark urine, or changes in her bowel habits.
Her appetite has improved since ending the fast, and she has had regular bowel movements.

She reports having experienced a similar episode of "yellow eyes" once before after recovering from a mild viral illness in high school, but never sought medical attention as the discoloration resolved within days.

encounters.cc: Two-month history of disturbed sleep with vivid, distressing nightmares occurring several times weekly.

lines: Two-month history of disturbed sleep with vivid, distressing nightmares occurring several times weekly.

The patient is a 23-year-old female with a known history of Gilbert syndrome, previously evaluated in Gastroenterology in January and April 2020 for intermittent scleral icterus, who presents with a two-month history of disturbed sleep.
She reports that several times a week she wakes suddenly during the night from vivid, distressing dreams in which she is being chased or threatened.
In the dreams, she often finds herself unable to move quickly, feeling as if her legs are weighed down, until the fear becomes so intense that she wakes up.
After waking, she feels alert and remembers the dream clearly but finds it difficult to fall back asleep.
She has begun drinking a glass of wine a few nights a week in an attempt to relax and get back to sleep.
Over the past few weeks, she has noticed increasing daytime fatigue, irritability, and difficulty concentrating on her coursework.
She says the sleep problems began not long after the end of a relationship with her boyfriend of over a year.
She denies loss of interest in activities, excessive guilt, or hopelessness, but acknowledges feeling anxious about falling asleep because she fears the nightmares will return.
She has not experienced panic attacks, flashbacks during the day, or avoidance of particular places or people.

encounters.cc: Low energy, difficulty concentrating, and increased tearfulness that began about a month ago following a breakup.

lines: Low energy, difficulty concentrating, and increased tearfulness that began about a month ago following a breakup.

This 24-year-old female with a history of Gilbert syndrome and prior psychiatric evaluation for disturbed sleep with vivid nightmares returns to the clinic with low energy, difficulty concentrating, and increased tearfulness.
She reports feeling emotionally "off" since breaking up with her partner of three years.
She says the breakup was amicable but unexpected, and since then, she has found herself ruminating over what went wrong and questioning her own worth.
She recently started a new job at a design firm and worries that her emotional state is beginning to affect her performance.
She describes herself as feeling "flat," with diminished interest in going out with friends, though she continues to go to work and complete her basic responsibilities at home.
She sleeps about six hours per night and has a normal appetite.
She denies suicidal thoughts, anhedonia, or feelings of hopelessness.
She states, "I know it's only been a few weeks, but I just don't feel like myself."

encounters.cc: Several days of tingling and aching pain in the right leg that began after starting long evening walks in new tight running shoes.

lines: Several days of tingling and aching pain in the right leg that began after starting long evening walks in new tight running shoes.
The patient is a 24-year-old female with Gilbert syndrome and prior psychiatric treatment for nightmare disorder and adjustment disorder who presents with right leg symptoms.
She reports that the symptoms began after she started taking long evening walks in new running shoes that feel tighter than her previous pair.
She describes a burning pain along the outer aspect of her right lower leg and top of her foot, which worsens with prolonged walking.
She denies any recent trauma, falls, or back pain.
She has also felt more fatigued lately due to final exams, eating poorly, and sleeping only 4–5 hours per night.
